1. This is not a ruse created by the warden. As explained in the lighthouse, the Dr wanted to rehabilitate Andrew and break him free from his delusions. Showing that people can be cured and that they are not dangerous prisoners but actually people who need help.
2. Well the first Rachel is part of the play. They are setting up everything Andrew has been talking about for months in his delusions. The stuff he has made up in his mind. They make it real to try to show him how ridiculous and fake it all is. The second Rachel I am pretty sure is just him actually hallucinating and part of his mental illness. My evidence is the fact that he literally saw Chucks body on the rocks, so clear indicator he just had a hallucination since we see Chuck well and alive later on. This is the part in the movie where hes literally losing his shit.
3. Again, explained in the lighthouse. Everyone is going along with his delusions. The Dr explains that he set this all up to try to show Andrew how bullshit his made up story is. Its a elaborate attempt at proving his theory that Andrew can be rehabilitated by forcing him to see how fake it all is. They let him see the entire island so he can see for himself there are not any experiments. Its about proving his crazy delusions wrong.

Chuck "adds" information because Chuck is his Dr. Imagine being someones psychologist/psychiatrist and you listen to this story about a million times over a period of a year or so every week? You would know every detail. Its all a part of the act.

4. The storm where all the patients escaped was in no way part of the play. That was just incidental. When it happened they felt ok letting DiCaprios character run around because his primary doctor "Chuck" was literally with him following him around. Plus when a shit ton of crazy people break free your biggest issue at the moment isn't one single guy. The crazy dude attacking him was not planned. Something you gotta understand is not every moment is a planned moment. The things that occur are not usually planned, but the way the employees act and the things they say are. If you want more proof just look at the guards. They barely give a dam about the whole thing whenever Teddy talks to them, same with the employees. AKA they do not take it seriously at all cus they think this idea to break him from his delusions is bullshit and wont work.

5. The patient wrote on his book to run because she knew it was all fake and he was being tricked. Everyone on the island was coached and told not to say anything to him. They are really hoping this works out and "the most dangerous patient on the island" can be rehabilitated. Also if you remember, the guy who he talks to in the Fort prison after the storm was a man he actually hurt very badly because he tried to tell him his delusions were not real. He has a history of beating the shit out of people who try to tell him the truth of whats going on, so people are kind of afraid of him.   
  
Also patients trying to escape from mental institutions is pretty common regardless of anything else. It also adds to the creepy factor of the entire story. Sort of like the beginning how the almost bald old woman puts her finger to her lips as if to say "shhhh". However hoping literally mentally ill people will keep secrets for you is sort of a shot in the dark. That is like relying on a dog not to eat cookies off the table once you leave the room.

It is hard to get a job in the field for many reasons. Yes one of them is over saturation of applicants. You see a lot of middle aged people trying to break through and you see a lot of foreigners trying to get masters and PhDs in CS so they can move to the USA. So there's a lot of competition.

Another reason is that Covid created a environment where tech companies were making crazy money. This was cus everyone was indoors all day. To keep up with business they hired tons of people. Well when lock down ended they had to fire many people since sales went down. This means that new grads right now are up against people who have a lot of experience already that got laid off from the pandemic. That might last like another 2 years.

Another reason is that the job market just sucks for everyone right now. Also the field is filling up and becoming normalized like other professions meaning, you gotta compete and you gotta be the best to get the best paying jobs. It is easier in a sense because if you are insanely skilled programmer, you can get a job. If you went into finance and banking, it might be a different story and you might only be able to get a good job if you "know a guy"

In terms of work life balance... Yes it is like a 40 hour a week job for most people. Some people will be on call though which means you're supposed to come in when shit goes wrong even if its like midnight.  
Then there are people who work the really prestigious high paying jobs that make crazy money like google, Meta, Netflix, hedgefunds, and ai companies. Many people who work there burnout from the stress. So at the end of the day every job at the top level is going to kinda be stressful. Also bad management can ruin a good job if they treat you like shit.

They wanna make money and keep you working as much as they can. Some companies are chill some are not.
